title: Cap. II: Augustine vs Pelagius; dogma already rejected — no fresh refutation
pass_a_gloss: Both are gathered from Augustine: the former from Epistle 89, where he brandishes an Anathema against the Pelagians on account of the aforesaid heresy: That which they say, that free choice suffices for a human to fulfill the Lord's precepts, is altogether to be anathematized, and to be detested with all execrations. The latter from On the Predestination of the Saints, book 1, chapter 18: God foresaw, says the Pelagian, who would be holy through the choice of free will, and therefore before the constitution of the world he elected them in that very foresight of his by which he foresaw them to be such. But because all theologians of every sect already reject Pelagius and this Pelagian dogma, or at least wish to seem to have rejected it, I will not make business for myself in refuting those things which no one dares openly to defend. Key lemmas: anathema; Epist. 89; De praedestinatione sanctorum; dogma Pelagianum.
pass_b_english: Augustine supplies both. First, Epistle 89, where he hurls anathema at the Pelagians for that heresy: their claim that free choice alone is enough to keep the Lord's commands is to be anathematized and cursed outright. Second, On the Predestination of the Saints 1.18: God foresaw, says the Pelagian, who would be holy by free will's choice, and so before the world's founding he elected them in that very foresight by which he foresaw them to be such. But since theologians of every party already reject Pelagius and this Pelagian dogma — or at least want to look as if they have — I will not waste effort refuting what no one dares openly defend.
source_text: Utrumque colligitur ex Augustino: prius ex Epist. 89. Ubi Anathema vibrat contra Pelagianos ob haeresin praedictam, Illud quod dicunt, sufficere homini liberum arbitrium ad dominica praecepta implenda, omnino anathematizandum est, & omnibus exsecrationibus detestandum. Posterius ex De praedestin. Sanctor. lib. 1. cap. 18. Praesciebat ergo, ait Pelagianus, qui futuri erant sancti per liberae voluntatis arbitrium, & ideo eos ante mundi constitutionem in ipsa sua praescientia, qua tales futuros esse praescivit, elegit. Sed quia Pelagium atque Pelagianum hoc dogma omnes omnium sectarum Theologi jam rejiciunt, aut saltem videri volunt rejecisse, non facessam mihi negotii in illis refellendis, quae nemo audet aperte propugnare.
